Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

r4subrisk (development version)

  • Add reconcile_risk_registers(), an item-level audit of what changed between two versions of a risk register (a prior vs current draft, or two assessors’ registers). It aligns rows by risk_id and labels each risk added, removed, changed, or unchanged; for changed risks it reports which fields differ (description, category, probability, impact, detectability, owner, mitigation, status) as a tidy field_changes audit, with prior and current values side by side. RPN movement is read from each register’s own stored rpn (nothing is recomputed or invented); it is a purely structural diff. This complements risk_trend() (trajectory over many milestones) with a line-by-line view of a single pair.
  • Fix the documented return value of compare_risk_registers(): rpn_changes is the tibble of all risks common to both registers (unchanged ones included, with a zero delta), not only those whose RPN changed.
  • Add risk_pareto(), a Pareto (“vital few”) prioritization of a register. It ranks risks by their stored RPN (recomputing nothing), reports each risk’s share and the running cumulative share of total RPN, and flags the smallest top run of risks that together carry a caller-supplied cumulative share (cum_cutoff, default 0.8, the usual Pareto 80 percent). The cutoff is a reporting convention over cumulative RPN share, not a risk, severity, or RPN threshold. plot_risk_pareto() draws the classic bar-plus-cumulative-line Pareto chart when ggplot2 is available.
  • Add write_risk_register() and read_risk_register() for a risk register import/export round-trip. Registers export to CSV (or xlsx when writexl / readxl are installed) as a faithful, human-readable snapshot. On import the file is rebuilt through create_risk_register(), so the canonical schema, RPN, and risk-level classification are recomputed from the assessed scores rather than trusted from the file; a write -> read cycle reproduces an equivalent register.
  • Add risk_trend(), which turns a named, ordered list of risk registers (one per submission milestone) into a tidy burndown tibble: per milestone the total RPN, mean RPN, number of risks, and open-critical count. The stored RPN and risk levels are reused as-is, so no scoring is recomputed. plot_risk_trend() draws the burndown as a ggplot line chart when ggplot2 is available.
  • Import %||% from rlang so the package works on its declared minimum R version (R >= 4.2); the operator only became part of base R in 4.4.0.
  • Fix the “Risk Management” vignette: the mitigation example now uses the probability, impact, and detectability columns that apply_mitigations() actually reads (previously *_residual columns were silently ignored, so the before/after comparison showed no change), and the configuration example no longer references the non-existent required_origins field.

r4subrisk 0.3.1

  • Metadata and documentation polish for CRAN submission; no user-facing changes.

r4subrisk 0.3.0

  • Add risk_monte_carlo(), which puts uncertainty on the FMEA scores. An RPN is built from three integer judgements, so a single number hides how confident the assessment is. The simulation samples each probability, impact, and detectability around its assessed value and reports the distribution of RPN, per risk and for the register as a whole, including a 90% interval and the probability that each risk is actually critical. The random state is set and restored per call when a seed is given, so results are reproducible without disturbing the caller’s RNG.

r4subrisk 0.2.0

  • Add risk_reduction_summary(), which quantifies the risk removed between two registers: total and mean RPN reduction, percentage reduction, and counts of risks reduced, downgraded, added, and resolved.
  • Add plot_risk_heatmap() and risk_heatmap_data() for the standard FMEA probability by impact heatmap, with an optional interactive plotly version.
  • Add a pluggable risk-model interface: risk_model() plus the pre-built risk_model_fmea(), risk_model_probability_impact(), and risk_model_ich_q9(). apply_risk_model() scores any set of risks to a normalized 0-100 value so alternative models feed the same Risk pillar.
  • Add vignette: “Case study: FMEA risk on a pilot submission”, a worked before-and-after mitigation walkthrough using the example risk register from r4subdata.
  • Clarified the package DESCRIPTION: “R4SUB” expands to “Ready for Submission” (previously “R for Regulatory Submission”, inconsistent with the rest of the ecosystem).

r4subrisk 0.1.1

  • Add vignette: “Risk Management with r4subrisk” covering create_risk_register(), compute_risk_scores(), apply_mitigations(), compare_risk_registers(), and evidence_to_risks() integration.
